place-value-1000-skill-01.target: I can explain that 100 is the same as ten tens and trade between tens and hundreds.
place-value-1000-skill-01.ifCorrect: You can do this: can explain that 100 is the same as ten tens and trade between tens and hundreds.
place-value-1000-skill-01.ifMissed: Practice this skill again. Watch for this mistake: Thinking 10 tens is 10 or 1,000, or not seeing a hundred flat as made of tens. Try this: Stack ten tens rods on a hundred flat and count by tens to 100.

place-value-1000-skill-02.target: I can tell how many hundreds, tens, and ones are in a three-digit number and the value of each digit.
place-value-1000-skill-02.ifCorrect: You can do this: can tell how many hundreds, tens, and ones are in a three-digit number and the value of each digit.
place-value-1000-skill-02.ifMissed: Practice this skill again. Watch for this mistake: Giving the digit instead of its value (the 4 in 249 is worth 4), or ignoring a zero (706 read as 76). Try this: Use base-ten blocks and a place-value chart; say the value aloud (“4 tens is 40”).

place-value-1000-skill-03.target: I can tell that 100, 200, … 900 are one to nine hundreds with 0 tens and 0 ones.
place-value-1000-skill-03.ifCorrect: You can do this: can tell that 100, 200, … 900 are one to nine hundreds with 0 tens and 0 ones.
place-value-1000-skill-03.ifMissed: Practice this skill again. Watch for this mistake: Writing 5 hundreds as 5 or 5,000, or 500 as “50 tens and 0 hundreds” without seeing both are true. Try this: Count hundred flats by 100s and write the number with zeros in the tens and ones places.

place-value-1000-skill-04.skill: Numerals, Number Names, and Expanded Form
place-value-1000-skill-04.target: I can read and write numbers to 1,000 as numerals, in words, and in expanded form.
place-value-1000-skill-04.ifCorrect: You can do this: can read and write numbers to 1,000 as numerals, in words, and in expanded form.
place-value-1000-skill-04.ifMissed: Practice this skill again. Watch for this mistake: Writing what is heard (“four hundred six” → 4006), or leaving out a zero place (400 + 6 → 46). Try this: Build the number with blocks first, then fill a place-value chart before writing it.
